On to what I'm here to talk about...
As I've seen some other people elsewhere say, my 2700x would hit these weird and fairly often MHz & temp spikes. Even sitting at idle, you'd see it peg REALLY hard and can sometimes even be felt while using the PC in the form of a micro-stutter.
However, as you do with a new PC, I've spent a few days in the BIOS trying to squeeze every last bit of performance I possibly can out of everything.
Ryzen's Precision Boost Overdrive seems to do really well on its own after setting a few things manually (TDC:114A -- EDC:168A -- PPT:1000W lol)
But those spikes were still bugging the hell out of me, mostly because I didn't know what was causing them.
Going through other forums and changing a bunch of values, as if I actually knew what I was doing, did... absolutely nothing.
However, today, I stumbled upon some of the pro overclocker's forums and they were talking about Ryzen's Infinity Fabric and how much your memory's latency can mess with it, specifically the way it can mess with the two separate core clusters interact with each other.
I already had my Geil Super Luce set to spec (3000MHz 16-18-18-36) but screwing with DRAM is always made to sound like the most awful experience imaginable.
I decided to give it a shot. Booted into BIOS, loaded up one of the higher profiles (3200MHz 18-20-20-36(8?)) and without touching the voltage, it booted up just fine, blah blah blah, ended up getting it to 3200MHz 16-18-18-36.
My core & temp spikes are completely gone.
My CPU is idling 3c cooler (didn't effect heavy load temps & MOS temp is ~1c higher)
There hasn't been any sort of stutter in any way.
And this may just be a false sense of accomplishment, but things genuinely seem to be snappier - even more so than a 16 logic core CPU already is.
I don't know, but I think I just unlocked the EXPECTED level of performance for the Ryzen Zen+ processor.
I'm also probably shooting myself in the foot by writing this too, because I haven't done any extended RAM tests, because, you know... Shut up.
Anyways, if you're rocking a Ryzen X-version and you've been having some of the problems people are reporting with them (really not that many people, but still)
Try what I did.
Overclocking My RAM Cooled My PC??

Overclocking the RAM on Ryzen makes the whole CPU faster. All the different parts of the CPU communicate with each other via Infinity Fabric. Infinity Fabric's speed is half of RAM speed. So, by overclocking your ram, you're also overclocking the Infinity Fabric, which makes the CPU work better when communicating between different parts.

More specifically, Zen is broken up into 4 core parts. If you have an 8 core CPU, there's two 4 core parts that have to communicate with each other via Infinity Fabric. By overclocking your ram, you're increasing how fast those two 4 core parts (CCX) can talk to eachother (as well as some other stuff).

Ryzen loves faster RAM and it's always worth it to set it up properly.
